source.notes: Photogrammetry scan of the Deutsches Museum's own Macintosh Plus (inventory number 2000-468, 'Hersteller: Apple Computer Corporation, Herstellung: Cupertino, California, 1987' per the museum's Sketchfab description; its online catalogue at https://digital.deutsches-museum.de/item/2000-468/ was down for maintenance when checked). Three parts: computer, keyboard, mouse, one 200k-face mesh with one 4096 px texture. glTF zip downloaded by the user from Sketchfab on 2026-10-09, 15 MB unpacked. Dates, price and dimensions from the English Wikipedia 'Macintosh Plus' infobox: released 16 January 1986 at US$2,599, discontinued 15 October 1990, 13.6 x 9.6 x 10.9 in (34.5 x 24.4 x 27.7 cm), 16.5 lb (7.5 kg). Wikidata Q1255728.

object.medium: Personal computer: beige plastic all-in-one case with built-in 9-inch monochrome display, separate keyboard and mouse
object.description: The Macintosh Plus of January 1986 is the first Macintosh in the original upright case to stay in production for years: the 1984 machine's 9-inch screen, mouse and windowed desktop, now with a megabyte of memory, a SCSI port and a keyboard with a numeric keypad. It sold until 1990, longer than any other classic Mac. This one belongs to the Deutsches Museum in Munich, which scanned it with its keyboard and mouse.
facts: At US$2,599 it cost more than the original 128K Macintosh, but could take four megabytes of memory, sixteen times as much.
The Plus introduced the SCSI port to the Macintosh, which made fast external hard disks possible for the first time.
Its 512 by 342 pixel black-and-white screen is the same one the 1984 Macintosh used, in the same case; only the badge and keyboard give the model away.
